node.label: Tandem
node.summary: An AI study planner that turns your syllabus and deadlines into a realistic weekly plan, then adapts when life happens.

node.label: Price-conscious free-tier trialists
node.summary: Students who will try new tools if there is a real free tier but balk at $8/month, compare against free tiers of Notion, Todoist, ChatGPT and MyStudyLife, and churn subscriptions regularly.

node.label: Time-starved outcome buyers
node.summary: Busy students who will pay readily if the tool demonstrably saves hours per week and cuts planning busywork.

node.label: Entrenched incumbent-tool users
node.summary: Long-time Notion/Todoist/MyStudyLife/ChatGPT users who already pay for a tool, demand painless import and export, and question whether an AI planner is just a wrapper.

node.label: Group-chat-driven adopters
node.summary: Students who adopt what their friends vouch for; switching stories from friends drive their decisions, mostly discovered via TikTok and word of mouth.

node.label: Privacy-first AI skeptics
node.summary: Students who have left tools over training on user content and require a clear privacy policy and proof the AI works before uploading coursework.

node.label: Privacy and data-training concerns
node.summary: Widespread refusal to upload study materials without a clear privacy policy; multiple users left incumbents over training on user content.

node.label: Subscription fatigue and $8 feeling steep
node.summary: Students resist another $8/month subscription, prefer one-time purchase, and benchmark against free tiers.

node.label: Heavy setup and learning curve
node.summary: Onboarding over five minutes is a dealbreaker; users spent weekends configuring Todoist/Notion/MyStudyLife and abandoned them.

node.label: Unreliable, gimmicky AI and crashes
node.summary: Tools that are confidently wrong or crash erode trust; the space is seen as full of demos that break on real use.

node.label: Switching cost: import/export and lock-in
node.summary: Users won't move without import from MyStudyLife/Todoist and fear being unable to export.

node.label: Weak mobile and offline support
node.summary: Most planning happens on phones; incumbent mobile apps are called unusable and offline use on commutes is needed.

node.label: Doubt it's more than a ChatGPT wrapper

node.label: Desire to automate planning busywork and save hours
node.summary: Strong demand for automation that incumbents only half deliver; saving a few hours a week is an instant buy.

node.label: Desire for a simple, decent planner
node.summary: Anticipation for a well-built, simple study planner; many follow new launches closely.

node.label: Planner incumbents racing to add AI amid price rises
node.summary: Notion, Todoist, ChatGPT and MyStudyLife reported raising prices while startups add AI features.

node.label: Data-policy backlash against incumbents
node.summary: All four named competitors face backlash over data policy changes, raising privacy expectations.

node.label: Rise of indie study planner tools
node.summary: Indie tools gaining ground against incumbents.

node.label: Youth subscription fatigue
node.summary: Surveys and posts report fatigue with recurring app fees among younger buyers.

node.label: AI hype fatigue
node.summary: Users tired of 'AI-powered' labels and gimmick tools.

node.label: Notion
node.summary: Feature-rich with a free tier but brutal learning curve, weak mobile, recent price rise and data-policy backlash.

node.label: MyStudyLife
node.summary: Category incumbent with a free tier, criticised for crashes, inaccuracy, unusable mobile app and training on user content; users leaving.

node.label: ChatGPT
node.summary: Default free alternative; users stick with it above $8 but report inaccuracy, crashes, poor mobile and data-policy concerns.

node.label: Todoist
